chunks: It has been narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام that he said:
"If a man dies while he has outstanding sawm (fasting) from the month of Ramadan, then whoever wishes from his family may make it up on his behalf."

key_terms.أَهْلِهِ: his family; the relatives who may perform the fasts on his behalf
key_terms.الصَّادِقِ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, from whom this hadith is narrated
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, whose obligatory fasts are meant here
key_terms.فَلْيَقْضِ: let him make up; to perform the missed fasts as qaḍāʾ
key_terms.مَاتَ: died; refers to the death of the person who owed the fasts

ai.seo_question: Can a family member make up missed Ramadan fasts for a deceased relative?
ai.summary: This hadith states that if a person dies while owing fasts from the month of Ramadan, a member of his family may perform the make-up fasts on his behalf. It indicates the legitimacy of fulfilling certain devotional obligations for the deceased through their relatives.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2009 - It has been narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that he said:
"If a man dies and has unfulfilled fasting from the Month of Ramadan, anyone from his family who wishes may make up the fasts on his behalf."
